changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Kamala Harris
metadata.description: Former US vice president whose latest detailed programme combines private enterprise with family cash credits, targeted price controls and reproductive rights, alongside AI safeguards and current calls for Senate oversight.
metadata.period: 2017–4 October 2026; 2024 platform and 2026 statements weighted most heavily
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 2017–4 October 2026; 2024 platform and 2026 statements weighted most heavily. Coalition measures are attributed cautiously. Modern hypothetical policies are labelled inferred, not claimed as direct statements. Research cutoff 4 October 2026; later views do not overwrite a former governing period.
metadata.role: Former Vice President of the United States; national political campaigner

axes.brief: Elections, judicial rights and independent legislative checks structure political legitimacy, reaffirmed in September 2026 campaigning.
axes.counterEvidence: Executive action remains important in her programme, but the current record explicitly calls for Senate constraint rather than unchecked presidential authority.

answers.rationale: Her 2026 campaigning locates political power in elections and voter participation.
Expert advice should serve elected institutions rather than replace public choice.
Equal citizenship and voting-rights advocacy reject educational qualifications for voting.
Her current appeal for Senate checks treats legislative independence as necessary to restrain executive abuse.
Competitive opposition is essential to the electoral strategy she advocates.
Her 2026 speech explicitly seeks an effective Senate check on the administration.
Her legal approach relies on courts enforcing constitutional rights even against executive action.
Unions are legitimate political participants, not an alternative authority selecting government instead of voters.
Political disagreement alone should not disqualify lawful opposition from competing.
Reproductive-rights ballot participation supports direct popular lawmaking with constitutional safeguards.
Her AI speech explicitly calls for executive and legislative cooperation rather than unilateral rule.
Constitutional accountability supports lawful removal for substantiated abuse.
Her electoral approach rejects unilateral postponement to protect an incumbent.
Voter accountability matters alongside stable representative terms and existing constitutional removal procedures.
Her criticism of executive abuse rejects government beyond public accountability.
Her opposition to presidential use of armed power for political retaliation supports civilian constitutional control.

axes.brief: Civil liberties and bodily autonomy coexist with a substantial public-safety and prosecution orientation.
axes.counterEvidence: Her prosecutorial record and border enforcement qualify an unrestricted-liberty interpretation; gun ownership is distinct from rejecting gun regulation.

answers.rationale: Marijuana reform and bodily autonomy favour liberty, while her law-enforcement approach retains restrictions on dangerous substances.
Judicially authorised serious-crime investigation fits her prosecutorial and constitutional approach.
Peaceful dissent deserves protection while proportionate limits can preserve transport and public safety.
Offensive criticism of powerful institutions remains protected unless a distinct unlawful harm is established.
Public-health regulation is legitimate, while reproductive autonomy limits coercion over exclusively personal health decisions.
Her AI privacy commitments oppose indiscriminate tracking, qualified by support for lawful intelligence and policing.
Preventing impaired driving harms fits her public-safety approach.
Independent judicial findings can justify narrowly limited preventative restrictions on credible threats.
Morally offensive expression remains legitimate when offence is the only claimed harm.
Anonymous participation supports dissent while enforceable protections against abuse and crime may require defined identification mechanisms.
Imminent danger may justify limited searches, but civil-rights protections constrain blanket or discriminatory stops.
Credible serious disorder can justify proportionate restrictions rather than treating every proposed assembly as immune.
Independent legal authorization normally protects home privacy, with urgent safety exceptions.
Accountability favours disclosure of misconduct, while genuine security and lawful confidentiality remain competing interests.
She explicitly defends personal firearm ownership while supporting background checks, red-flag laws and some weapon bans.
Her legal-rights framework favours independent court oversight even when security detention is justified.

axes.brief: Plural civic identity and equitable access coexist with shared institutions and integration.
axes.counterEvidence: Equal inclusion does not imply separate communities should supersede shared civic responsibilities.

answers.rationale: Her pluralist civic account resists automatically subordinating minority practices to the dominant culture.
Inclusion and equitable services justify reasonable cultural and linguistic accommodation.
Shared civic responsibilities matter without requiring abandonment of inherited customs.
Immigrants can retain cultural identity while becoming full civic participants.
English access is useful, while multilingual services protect participation by citizens and residents with varied backgrounds.
Her public inclusion of Indigenous recognition supports acknowledgment in national ceremonies.
Shared heritage can receive support, but public provision should not exclude minority traditions simply because they are smaller.
Her national political programme relies on shared citizenship rather than separate identities taking priority over common life.
A common civic calendar can coexist with reasonable accommodation of minority observance.
Several traditions can legitimately form part of national identity.
Civic integration supports participation in shared institutions without demanding cultural erasure.

Her equitable-services programme supports community languages on public signs alongside accessible shared information. This inference concerns official public communication, rather than merely permission for private linguistic expression.
Families can transmit heritage without a state requirement to favour the dominant identity.
Religious accommodation is reasonable when identification and concrete security requirements remain effective.
Her equality and inclusion approach recognises a plural national community.
Integration should focus on civic participation rather than cultural replacement as its principal goal.

axes.brief: Her latest detailed border programme combines tougher enforcement with regulated legal pathways and family protection.
axes.counterEvidence: Her 2019 decriminalisation position differs from the tougher 2024 border programme; the latter is weighted more heavily as the latest detailed platform.

answers.rationale: Her border proposal supports enforcement thresholds for irregular arrivals, while lawful migration includes several administered pathways. An emergency border trigger is not a strict overall annual immigration cap, so enforcement and wider lawful opportunity support a mixed assessment.
Opportunity-based migration is valuable but does not alone establish an unrestricted entry entitlement.
Family and humanitarian pathways remain legitimate alongside skilled migration.
Family unity deserves a lawful route, with regulated eligibility and security checks.
Protection should depend on persecution and need rather than cultural resemblance or immediate workforce usefulness.
Her tougher border programme coexists with support for pathways for established undocumented residents.
Employer demand matters alongside labour protections, border capacity and lawful admission.
Service pressure is relevant, but immigration also contributes labour and economic opportunity.
Family reunification deserves weight within a managed legal system rather than automatic exemption from all planning.
A job offer supports eligibility while security, qualifications and labour standards remain relevant.

Protection and humanitarian pathways permit settlement without either employer or family sponsorship. Family reunion itself meets the family-sponsor condition, so it cannot be the reason for disagreeing with this question.

She favours pathways for educated talent but also regulated immigration eligibility. Graduation can support access to a route without automatically awarding permanent residence; these are different thresholds, and her broader programme balances the educational preference with additional conditions.
Humanitarian urgency can justify exceptions, while her recent border proposal places substantial weight on processing capacity.
Equal protection rejects cultural similarity as a general preference among refugees.
Basic and lawful-resident protections matter, while public-programme eligibility can differ by immigration status.
Diversity is valuable, but admission priorities also concern family, protection, work and administrative capacity.

axes.brief: Alliance commitments and strong deterrence coexist with diplomacy and accountable use of force.
axes.counterEvidence: Support for allies and military capability prevents treating diplomatic language as pacifism.

answers.rationale: Her alliance and deterrence posture accepts force for wider security interests beyond direct territorial attack.
Diplomacy should usually precede force, though credible threats and allied obligations can require faster action.
Her defence posture favours maintaining substantial military capability despite significant cost.
Credible imminent threats can justify pre-emptive defence under lawful and proportionate conditions.
Alliance support and counterterrorism roles go beyond a strict retaliatory-only doctrine.
Her programme relies on professional armed forces rather than compulsory male service.
Concessions may avert war, but she does not subordinate allied security to every immediate peace proposal.
Her military-AI principles require legal review and accountable use; efficiency alone is insufficient for autonomous killing decisions.
Her global alliance role requires capabilities beyond repelling invasion.
Defence of allies remains legitimate even when it risks armed conflict.
Her security approach accepts sustained overseas capability when justified by alliances and concrete missions.
Negotiation generally offers a preferable route to resolving territorial disputes without war.
Credible force can support deterrence and diplomacy rather than being excluded from bargaining.
Preventing escalation matters while her alliance commitments also give weight to credible resolve.
Necessary intelligence gathering is acceptable despite diplomatic risk, subject to legal safeguards.
Verified reciprocal reductions can improve security without undermining legitimate deterrence.

axes.brief: Cooperative international action is accepted within constitutional national authority.
axes.counterEvidence: International AI cooperation does not imply surrender of every domestic constitutional decision to external bodies.

answers.rationale: Constitutional democratic authority remains central alongside international commitments.
Agreed global AI, climate and security rules can legitimately constrain unilateral national action.
Domestic constitutional protections and international legal obligations both carry weight.
Durable alliances are valued even when they limit unilateral policy choices.
Membership rests on national consent, although withdrawal should account for treaty duties and strategic consequences.
International accountability matters while the US constitutional and security framework limits unrestricted external jurisdiction.
National interests coexist with shared climate, rights and security responsibilities rather than invariably prevailing.

She supports common action on climate and transboundary risks while retaining national constitutional authority. International cooperation and AI safety coordination are not themselves a transfer of environmental decision-making authority; the judgment is conditional on the institution and its powers.

Her alliance commitments support coordinated diplomacy, while US foreign decisions remain nationally accountable. Joining ordinary alliances is distinct from joining a bloc that requires a common foreign policy, so cooperation and independent discretion both matter.
Agreed human-rights duties can justify domestic legislative changes through constitutional process.
Her economic programme retains the dollar and national monetary institutions.
Joint international programmes may pool resources and oversight for shared goals.
National border management remains important while lawful refugee duties and international cooperation constrain exclusivity.
Trade rules are useful when they preserve worker, environmental and security safeguards.
Her internationalism concerns cooperation rather than merging the United States into a broader federation.
Credible common rules require accepting some near-term costs beyond immediate national advantage.

axes.brief: Explicit capitalism and public-private delivery coexist with health programmes and infrastructure investment.
axes.counterEvidence: Public financing is not equivalent to provider nationalisation; her 2024 economic programme explicitly describes itself as capitalist.

answers.rationale: Her explicit capitalist programme retains predominantly private commercial ownership.
Public utilities can be effective, while regulated private provision also fits her mixed-economy approach.
Private ownership is acceptable when public operation brings no clear access or accountability advantage.
Public alternatives can address market gaps, but her innovation programme primarily mobilises private enterprise.
Her recent health programme builds on mixed insurance and providers rather than universally nationalising delivery.

Public passenger-rail investment and Amtrak ownership coexist with passenger services operating over privately owned shared tracks. This supports a mixed infrastructure-ownership arrangement; investment in passenger service alone does not establish public ownership of every track it uses.
Genuine savings can justify contracting where service quality, worker protections and accountability remain intact.
Public lending tools can support underserved firms without establishing a general public retail-banking preference.
Ordinary commercial assets may be sold when no strategic public purpose requires ownership.
Her housing programme emphasises supply incentives and assistance alongside public provision rather than a predominant public landlord sector.
Regulation and public-private partnerships can protect strategic objectives without universal state acquisition.
Resource regulation and taxation are more consistent with her programme than general public ownership of extraction.
Private local-service delivery can be legitimate where accountability and equivalent quality are secured.
Strategic value can justify retention, while immediate receipts alone do not settle ownership.
Losses warrant reform but public-service obligations can justify continuing support rather than automatic sale.
Independent public broadcasting merits support, but this does not necessarily require direct state ownership.

axes.brief: Broad tariffs are opposed while domestic manufacturing and strategic trade safeguards are supported.
axes.counterEvidence: Strategic tariffs and subsidies differ from universal trade protection; opposition to broad tariffs does not mean no trade restrictions.

answers.rationale: She opposes broad import tariffs while retaining strategic trade remedies.
Wider market access and competitive prices can justify liberalisation with worker adjustment support.
Domestic manufacturing incentives give domestic procurement some weight even when costs are higher.
Affordable foreign inputs support business competitiveness subject to security and standards.
Essential resilience can justify selected restrictions without general rejection of cheaper imports.
Her approach favours negotiated and strategic liberalisation rather than automatic unilateral tariff elimination.

Targeted industrial investment does not itself restrict imports. The Biden-Harris administration retained strategic tariffs, but her opposition to broad tariffs and emphasis on subsidies leave a mixed inference about temporary infant-industry restrictions imposed despite higher consumer prices.
Foreign investment is welcome subject to national-security and fair-competition review.
Agricultural access and affordable food matter alongside domestic producer adjustment.
Worker training and competitiveness are generally preferable to permanently protecting every declining producer.
Proportionate remedies can address unfair barriers while broad retaliation risks raising household costs.
Equal taxation fits fair competition, with distinct targeted remedies for proven distortions.
Demonstrable foreign subsidies may justify measured restrictions to protect fair competition.
Agreements can reduce barriers when labour, environmental and resilience requirements are preserved.
Strategic security can justify blocking particular takeovers without rejecting foreign investment generally.
Cross-border digital commerce is valuable, subject to enforceable privacy, consumer and AI safety requirements.

axes.brief: Private markets are supplemented by targeted industrial investment, wage floors and consumer protection.
axes.counterEvidence: Her price-gouging and prescription proposals are targeted rather than general production or price planning.

answers.rationale: Her entrepreneurial programme leaves ordinary production choices to private firms.
Public investment and regulation do not imply mandatory national output quotas.
Market pricing remains the normal mechanism with targeted action against abuses and essential unaffordability.
Manufacturing and innovation investment deliberately favour strategic sectors.
New firms and market demand are central to her opportunity-economy programme.
Prescription-cost limits and action against price gouging support intervention in particular essential markets.
Startup incentives support entry without requiring official proof of a production need.
Public lending can address financing gaps, while ordinary credit allocation remains commercially determined.
Open investment supports entrepreneurship, subject to sanctions and financial safeguards.
Her manufacturing and startup programme uses selective subsidies and tax incentives.
Financial innovation may be useful, while stable public money and consumer safeguards constrain unrestricted private currencies.
Higher wage floors fit her labour and middle-class programme.
Bargaining and statutory protections coexist with negotiated wages rather than national wage schedules.
Monetary independence fits her market framework more closely than interest rates dictated by a production plan.
Housing affordability can justify targeted regulation, while supply expansion and market building incentives remain central.
Coordinated strategic investment does not mean routine national planning of ordinary production and distribution.

axes.brief: Progressive financing and family support seek broader opportunity within a market economy.
axes.counterEvidence: Support for enterprise and wealth-building constrains any claim that her goal is equal disposable incomes.

answers.rationale: Progressive finance and family support aim to reduce material disadvantage while preserving enterprise incentives.
Large unequal gains can justify progressive contributions beyond merely financing bare necessities.

Her proposed expanded refundable child tax credits strengthen family cash income and are linked to progressive financing. These direct income measures, rather than health coverage alone, support a stronger minimum-income floor.
Her opportunity agenda extends beyond subsistence to reducing unequal access and building household wealth.
Affluent households should contribute more while middle-class tax relief remains a priority.
Earned rewards matter alongside obligations to fund shared opportunity.
Limiting inherited advantage is consistent with progressive taxation, qualified by her emphasis on families building wealth.
Work incentives matter, while caregiving, disability and insecure employment qualify rigid universal time limits.
Taxing wealthy households more fits her programme, but a broad recurring net-wealth levy is not its principal instrument.
Expanded health and child support are not subordinated simply to keeping benefits modest.

Refundable child and earnings credits support families beyond emergency subsistence. That supplies qualified evidence for adequate cash participation; maternal healthcare services alone would not establish the level of income benefits.
Unmet health and family needs can take precedence over additional tax cuts.
Refundable credits and support for low-paid families fit her economic programme.
Progressive marginal tax rates are incompatible with treating every additional dollar alike across income levels.
Housing access warrants public investment, but broad compulsory land redistribution is not her preferred instrument.
Family tax credits and coverage support extend beyond households already unable to meet basic needs.

axes.brief: Civil rights are justified independently of personal religious belief while faith communities remain legitimate civic participants.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal faith and outreach to clergy do not establish a clerical veto, legislative review office or religious family-law authority.

answers.rationale: Her reproductive-rights argument explicitly separates personal faith from binding civil decisions.
Religious teachings should not be a privileged official source controlling everyone else's rights.
Individuals may consult clergy voluntarily, while government policy does not require clerical permission.
Equal religious citizenship weighs against constitutionally founding the state on one selected faith.
Schools can explain beliefs without using public authority to recruit pupils into a religion.
Government-directed faith cultivation conflicts with freedom of conscience and equal citizenship.
Civil institutions determine enforceable rights rather than clerical rulings.
Faith leaders can participate in consultation without a privileged official review office.
Civic religious expression can be inclusive, while compulsory organised worship would exclude nonbelievers.
Funding useful community services differs from funding persuasion into religious belief.
Official endorsement of one religion risks unequal civic standing.
Shared holidays can remain customary, while explicit recognition of one faith as predominant raises neutrality concerns.
Religious office alone should not confer government representation.
Special religious exemptions beyond ordinary charitable treatment require stronger justification than personal faith.
Civil marriage rights should not depend on religious approval.
Religious family decisions should not override civil equality and ordinary legal safeguards.

axes.brief: Reproductive freedom, marriage equality and inclusive social recognition take priority over restrictive traditions.
axes.counterEvidence: Her broad rights agenda does not imply rejecting every voluntary custom or parental role.

answers.rationale: Her civil-rights programme supports substantial change to exclusionary customs.
Tradition does not automatically outweigh equal rights and contemporary values.
Diverse families deserve equal social recognition.
Sex-role prescriptions conflict with her equal-opportunity and gender-equality approach.
She explicitly defends marriage equality as a right.
Caring family relationships matter more than privileging one married household structure.
Her reproductive-freedom programme strongly supports accepting early abortion choices.
Parents deserve involvement but not an unlimited veto over inclusive public education.
Same-sex couples should receive equal social acceptance as adoptive parents under child-welfare standards.
Adult dress is principally personal choice rather than a single inherited modesty norm.
Respectful language should adapt to identity, with separate questions about legal compulsion.
Established customs deserve consideration rather than automatic priority over inclusive alternatives.
Equal acceptance extends to adults departing from traditional sex roles.
Popular rights reforms should not be postponed simply because an institution is longstanding.
Inclusive education should acknowledge varied orientations and gender identities despite traditional disagreement.
Heritage can be meaningful voluntarily without requiring every obsolete custom to be maintained.

axes.brief: Technological benefits are pursued alongside explicit AI safety, privacy and nondiscrimination protections.
axes.counterEvidence: Brain implants and embryo enhancement are explicitly inferred from risk and rights principles, not presented as direct personal proposals.

answers.rationale: Her AI programme promotes benefits while requiring safety oversight rather than treating early promise as sufficient for broad use.
Staged deployment and substantial risk evidence fit her safety-testing and reporting approach.
Infrastructure and housing expansion matter, while lasting ecological loss requires assessment and mitigation.
Long-term medical safety should be studied, with proportionate exceptions for urgent needs.
Productivity-enhancing AI can be adopted alongside workers' rights, retraining and safeguards.
Environmental protection and housing needs require case-specific balance rather than blanket priority for either.
Climate and scientific innovation make regulated cultivated-meat adoption plausible, subject to health and ecological monitoring.
Her health and AI safety framework supports research-only healthy-person implants until strong long-term evidence exists.
Technology investment and efficiency both matter; her approach does not rely solely on unproven large-scale solutions.
Poorly understood serious environmental effects justify delay while relevant evidence is gathered.
Adult consent supports choice, while invasive enhancement creates safety concerns beyond minimal initial testing.
Her AI emphasis on patient harms and discrimination supports strong reliability evidence across groups before routine diagnostic use.
Irreversible inherited enhancement requires a more cautious ethical threshold than ordinary medical research.
Environmental safeguards support long-term ecosystem evidence before extensive modified-crop use.
Her housing-supply and infrastructure agenda gives development substantial weight when preservation directly conflicts.
Plausible irreversible harm warrants strong evidence of low risk before deployment despite early benefits.

axes.brief: National rights and social guarantees coexist with protected state institutions and local implementation.
axes.counterEvidence: National reproductive rights override some state restrictions without eliminating all constitutional federalism.

answers.rationale: Constitutional state powers deserve protection except where they violate national rights.
Federal supremacy applies within defined powers, while courts and reserved state authority constrain unilateral national claims.
Her constitutional union does not grant unilateral secession on a simple regional vote.
National reproductive and civil rights can justify overriding obstructive regional policies.
State constitutions are compatible with national constitutional guarantees.
Federal enforcement serves national offences without replacing ordinary state and local police governance.
National health and social guarantees require redistribution across regions rather than retaining most local receipts.
National rights and educational access matter while states retain substantial curriculum authority.
States can vary taxes within constitutional limits without negating shared national programmes.
Common national employment protections prevent regional competition through weaker basic rights.
Council arrangements should not normally need federal permission, subject to state law and protected rights.
Her national health-rights approach supports common minimum coverage rather than entirely regional entitlements.
Indigenous institutions deserve meaningful local authority within national rights protections.
National coordination can limit destructive tax competition undermining shared services.
Region-confined land decisions can remain regional when no national rights or spillovers are implicated.
Major cross-regional disasters justify nationally directed coordination and resources.

axes.brief: Opportunity, representation and unequal social conditions receive substantial causal weight while individual biological variation is retained.
axes.counterEvidence: Maternal-health disparity claims concern unequal outcomes and research priorities, not proof that all traits are environmentally determined.

answers.rationale: Her opportunity and maternal-health agenda recognises powerful formative effects of surroundings and access.

Her opportunity programme treats education and unequal access as important explanations of achievement differences. It supports a modest inference against inherited national intelligence as the main account, without mistaking an equality commitment for scientific proof.
Gender barriers and social expectations receive substantial explanatory weight in her equal-opportunity programme.
Health research recognises biology while unequal stress exposure reflects social conditions; both deserve causal weight.
Investment in education and opportunity assumes experiences can reshape interests and aspirations.
Disposition affects risk-taking while incentives, insecurity and learning also matter; neither universally predominates.
Her coalition and inclusion approach assumes cooperative habits develop through institutions and shared experience.
Empathy involves individual disposition and learned perspective, with civil-rights education strengthening the latter.
Educational and developmental support treat attention as responsive to surroundings rather than simply fixed inheritance.
Moral reactions can involve predispositions and learned social norms; her legal values alone do not settle comparative causation.
Her concern with bias assumes threat perceptions can be socially learned and corrected.
Biomedical and social supports recognise interacting determinants of temperament rather than a universal single-source explanation.
Her concern with cultural representation makes socially learned beauty preferences a plausible moderate inference, without excluding biology.

Her racial-equity programme emphasises social conditions and institutional treatment in explaining crime disparities. The inference is qualified because policy does not establish every statistical causal contribution.

Her developmental and opportunity framework treats self-regulation as learnable. This supports a moderate environmental inference rather than a scientific assertion that inherited influences have no role.
Her equal-opportunity approach treats expectations and structural barriers as causal, rather than women's lower economic worth.

review.notes: Independent all-240 review of exact statements, with primary speeches and the September 2026 public remarks checked. Retained 2024 proposals as the last detailed platform rather than inventing a new 2026 administration. Corrected emergency border thresholds versus an overall annual cap, employer-or-family sponsorship, graduation as a route versus automatic residency, and public signs versus private expression. Corrected common action versus transferred environmental authority and alliances versus mandatory common foreign policy. Distinguished rail investment from ownership and cash credits from in-kind healthcare, and moderated unsupported causal certainty. Firearm ownership is consistent with her stated personal-defence position and regulation. Hypothetical technology and human-trait answers remain explicit inferences. Neutral values identify competing commitments; no similarity tuning. Independent close-neighbour review on 2026-10-04 compared exact answers, periods and policy mechanisms with barack-obama revision 1. Specific corrections and retention reasons are recorded in review.similarity; no score tuning was used. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.

similarity.reason: Retain both revision 1 profiles after independent exact-question comparison. Obama is assessed on enacted presidential conduct in 2009–2017; Harris is assessed on her later vice-presidential record, detailed 2024 programme and corroborating 2026 statements, without treating proposals as enactments. Their shared constitutional democracy, mixed economy and social-rights commitments explain close aggregate scores. Distinct evidence includes Obama’s TPP tariff-removal agenda, Iran nuclear bargaining and bulk-surveillance reform, versus Harris’s targeted affordability controls, expanded refundable family credits, more central reproductive-rights guarantees and explicit modern AI safety emphasis. In the bank these produce differences on trade14, military07, planning06, redistribution03, progressive07 and innovation02/12. Some one-step differences remain cautious inferences, not claims of radically different ideologies. The review corrected the tariff-versus-subsidy rationale and clarified passenger-track ownership; no answer was changed to reduce resemblance. Axis aggregation discards these item and period distinctions, so a close score is not duplication.
